benefits: Ingest is robust against non-media files in directories
Pipeline no longer fails on directories containing logs, READMEs, or temp files
Idempotent ingestion regardless of directory contents
INGEST-002.problem: Ingest currently aborts the entire directory when it encounters a non-media file that ffprobe cannot probe (only metadata.json is currently skipped, and subtitle files are handled as sidecars). Non-media files like logs, READMEs, or temp files cause ProbeFile() to return an error, failing the ingest.
INGEST-002.proposal: During ingestion, bypass ALL non-media files. Files that ffprobe cannot probe (and are not subtitle sidecars) should be skipped with a logged warning, and the ingest should continue processing the remaining files. Only genuine media files (and subtitle sidecars) should be recorded in the MediaUnit.
INGEST-002.outcome: Implemented. ingest.Ingest logs WARN and continues on probe error for non-media, non-subtitle files (ingest.go:55-58). Removed fmt import. Added TestIngest_NonMediaFilesSkipped verifying mixed media/subtitle/non-media directory ingestion succeeds with video stream.
tests: TestIngest_NonMediaFilesSkipped — ingest skips non-media files and continues processing the directory
INGEST-002.title: Bypass non-media files during ingest

benefits: Files with non-standard names are processed instead of silently skipped

INGEST-001.problem: Files with names not starting with digits (e.g. 'MyShow_E01.mkv') are silently skipped by the pipeline. The ingest phase rejects units whose filenames lack leading-digit product IDs, causing EventUnitFailed and zero output for those directories.
INGEST-001.proposal: When no filename starts with a digit, assign synthetic ID 9999 to the unit. FindByID(9999) misses metadata, fallbackProduct(dirname, 9999) kicks in. Pipeline processes the unit end-to-end with EventUnitDone.
INGEST-001.outcome: Implemented. Added SyntheticID constant (9999) and Synthetic bool field to MediaUnit. Both ingest.ExtractID and callname.ExtractID return SyntheticID instead of error for non-digit filenames. BuildInputName falls back to SyntheticID. Pipeline logs warning when Synthetic is true. All domain tests updated (TestExtractID, TestNewMediaUnit, TestBuildInputName). Pipeline integration test added (TestRunOnce_SyntheticID). Build, vet, test, and lint all pass.
tests: TestExtractID_NonDigitFilename — returns SyntheticID (9999) instead of error

TestRunOnce_SyntheticID — pipeline processes synthetic unit with EventUnitDone

benefits: Pipeline detects metadata.json changes between scan passes and reloads it transparently
Long-running pipelines process new episodes/movies added to the catalog without restart
No silent stale-catalog processing
METADATA-001.problem: Pipeline loads metadata.json exactly once at startup. For long-running pipelines, external updates to metadata.json (new episodes, corrected titles, added movies) are not reflected; the pipeline uses the stale startup snapshot.
METADATA-001.proposal: On each scan pass in the Run() loop, stat metadata.json and reload if mtime changed. Reload is atomic under write-lock; on failure, log warning and fall back to previous snapshot.
METADATA-001.outcome: Implemented. Repository gained metadataPath and lastMod fields; New() stats file and stores lastMod. Reload() stats file, compares mtime, reloads on change under write-lock, logs INFO on reload. Pipeline calls Reload() before RunOnce() in Run() loop via type assertion. Tests: TestRepository_Reload_Success, TestRepository_Reload_FailureFallback, TestRepository_Reload_Untouched. All tests pass with race detector; live test passes.
tests: TestRepository_Reload_Success — reload triggers on mtime change and serves new products
TestRepository_Reload_FailureFallback — corrupt JSON reload fails, repo serves old data
TestRepository_Reload_Untouched — Reload() returns (false, nil) when untouched
METADATA-001.title: Hot-reload metadata.json during long-running pipeline

benefits: Windows paths in logs use forward slashes, consistent with Unix paths

LOG-001.problem: On Windows, path values logged via the structured logger appear with escaped backslashes (e.g. \\192.168.31.4\buffer\...). The JSON file handler and text handler both use strconv.Quote which doubles backslashes, making paths hard to read and grep.
LOG-001.proposal: Add a shared normalizePath helper that replaces \ with /. Wire it into the JSON handler via ReplaceAttr (key matches 'path', 'dir', 'file') and into the text handler via formatAttrValue. Add tests for both handlers.
LOG-001.outcome: Implemented. Added normalizePath and isPathKey helpers in internal/infra/logging/logger.go. JSON handler uses ReplaceAttr to normalize path/dir/file string values. Text handler formatAttrValue takes key and normalizes matching keys. Tests added: TestCustomHandler_PathNormalization, TestNewFileHandler_PathNormalization. All tests pass with race detector; logging package lint clean.
tests: TestCustomHandler_PathNormalization — text handler normalizes input_path/dir/file, leaves non-path note unchanged
TestNewFileHandler_PathNormalization — JSON handler normalizes backslashes in path/dir attributes
LOG-001.title: Normalize Windows paths to forward slashes in log output
